quotes.text: So the concept of administrative tiering is in a nutshell. We box things into different administrative zones to prevent those nasty escalations or lateral movements from within Active Directory itself.
quotes.speaker: Viktor Hedberg
quotes.why: A compact definition of AD tiering given in direct answer to the host's question.

quotes.text: Main thing here is don't turn off anything. It's better to unplug things like the network cable, isolated network wise, but don't turn the systems off.
quotes.speaker: Viktor Hedberg
quotes.why: Clear, practical incident response advice that preserves forensic evidence.

quotes.text: you can use the PAM solution that targets it towards, you know, tier one administration. But because that's where you're going to have the bulk of your administrative users anyway. Don't let it touch your tier zero resources.
quotes.speaker: Viktor Hedberg
quotes.why: A concrete recommendation on where PAM belongs in a tiered model.

quotes.text: Maybe we shouldn't look at which tool to buy to help us prevent this. We should actually work with the basics first to get those in line, because we can add tools later that can help us maintain those basics later on down the line.
quotes.speaker: Viktor Hedberg
quotes.why: Viktor's closing takeaway: security hygiene before buying more tools.

takeaways: Administrative tiering boxes domain controllers, Entra Connect, PKI and similar systems into tier zero and blocks high-privilege accounts from logging on to lower tiers, limiting credential exposure.
Privileged access workstations combined with authentication policy silos and remote administration tools mean admin credentials are only usable on one device and are not left behind on servers.
Get the security basics right first, such as blocking domain admins from logging on everywhere, before adding PAM, PIM or other tools, and keep on-prem administration independent of the cloud.
hook: Active Directory is far from dead, and a single compromised device can still hand attackers the whole domain. In this conversation for IT admins and security teams, Viktor Hedberg explains AD tiering, privileged access workstations and why getting the basics right beats buying another security tool.
